title: Infrared Thermography and Platform Vibratory Protocol
author: Eloá Moreira-Marconi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wqhfdt6

steps.title: Select eligible participants
steps.instruction: Recruit individuals aged 20–45 years who are healthy; exclude anyone with joint pain or implants, musculoskeletal diseases, vertigo, or any clinical condition that could pose risk or discomfort during whole‑body vibration exercise.

steps.title: Randomize participants and blind assessors
steps.instruction: Assign participants to the three experimental conditions using colored cards; ensure that both the outcome assessors and the participants are unaware of the order of vibration frequencies.

steps.title: Acclimate participants for skin temperature
steps.instruction: Allow each participant a 15‑minute acclimation period in the testing room before any measurements to stabilize skin temperature (Tsk).

steps.title: Conduct pre‑session interview and record anthropometrics
steps.instruction: Interview each participant about caffeine intake, nicotine smoking, and sports training performed in the four hours preceding the session; then measure body mass and height and calculate body‑mass index (BMI).

steps.title: Prepare laboratory environment and equipment
steps.instruction: Set the laboratory (LAVIMPI, UERJ) to an ambient temperature of 25.5 ± 0.35 °C and relative humidity of 50.5 ± 2.16 %; schedule the session between 1 pm and 5 pm; have participants wear shorts, a t‑shirt, and remain barefoot; place the Power Plate pro5™ (Power Plate International Ltd, The Netherlands) in the testing area.

steps.title: Configure infrared camera and software
steps.instruction: Mount a FLIR Systems E40 infrared camera (sensor 160 × 120 px, NETD 70 mK at 30 °C, repeatability ±2 %) with emissivity set to 0.98; position it approximately 90° to the participant, 2 m from the vibration platform, and adjust its height to 10 cm below the right popliteal line for each participant; use FLIR ResearchIR Max software version 4.40.4.17 (Sweden) for image capture.

steps.title: Attach accelerometer and verify vibration parameters
steps.instruction: Fix a three‑axial accelerometer (Vibration Datalogger DT‑178A, Ruby Electronics, USA) to the base of the platform; confirm that 30 Hz at 1.20 mm amplitude yields 2.22 g (21.73 m s⁻²) and 50 Hz at 0.77 mm amplitude yields 4.40 g (43.11 m s⁻²).

steps.title: Perform vibration bouts in squat position
steps.instruction: For each participant, execute three 60‑second bouts separated by 90‑second rests; during every bout the participant assumes a squat on the platform with 130° knee flexion (checked with a manual goniometer), feet aligned with the shoulders, and arms at the sides. Apply the three conditions in random order: (a) no vibration (0 Hz), (b) WBVE 30 Hz with 1.20 mm amplitude, (c) WBVE 50 Hz with 0.77 mm amplitude.

substeps.instruction: Start 60‑second bout of the assigned condition.
Allow 90‑second rest before the next bout.

steps.title: Acquire and process infrared images
steps.instruction: Automatically record the posterior lower limbs for the full 60‑second bout at 30 frames s⁻¹ (total 1800 frames); split the frames into five equal ranges of 360 frames (12 s each) representing mean times of 6, 18, 30, 42, and 54 s; compute the average image of each range; use a focal line to keep the same regions of interest (ROI) across all frames—left/right thighs, knees, calves, and heels.

substeps.instruction: Record 1800 frames at 30 fps for 1 min.
Average each block to obtain images for 6, 18, 30, 42, and 54 s.
Apply the focal line to the predefined ROI (both legs).
